title: The Combustion Cell: A Multidisciplinary Review of the Causes, Mechanisms, and Mitigation Strategies for Lithium-Ion Battery Fires
content: The ubiquitous integration of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) into modern society, powering applications from portable electronics to grid-scale energy storage and electric mobility, has been paralleled by a growing concern over their safety. The high energy density that makes LIBs so advantageous also renders them susceptible to catastrophic failure modes, most notably fire and explosion. This review provides a comprehensive and multidisciplinary analysis of the phenomenon of battery fires. We begin by delineating the fundamental root causes of thermal runaway, the critical event precipitating combustion, including mechanical abuse, electrical abuse, thermal abuse, and manufacturing defects. The review then delves into the intricate mechanisms of thermal runaway, tracing the sequence of exothermic reactions from Solid Electrolyte Interphase (SEI) decomposition to the violent reactions of cathode materials and electrolyte. A detailed examination of the complex combustion chemistry of LIBs is presented, highlighting the roles of gaseous, liquid, and solid components as fuels and the generation of toxic and flammable effluents. The propagation of failure within a battery module or pack is discussed, underscoring the challenges in containing single-cell incidents. We systematically catalog and critically evaluate the current state-of-the-art mitigation strategies, spanning intrinsic safety approaches (novel electrolytes, solid-state batteries, advanced electrode materials) and extrinsic safety systems (battery management systems, thermal management systems, and fire suppression technologies). Finally, the review identifies persistent knowledge gaps and outlines future research directions, emphasizing the need for multi-scale modeling, advanced diagnostics, and the development of inherently safe next-generation battery chemistries. This work aims to serve as a foundational reference for researchers and engineers across academia and industry, fostering the development of safer energy storage systems.
